x: The 3000 metres event saw Len Eyre come home in first place followed by Paget and Gordon Pirie and Ray Tooby ran well to finish 5th and was clocked to do 8 min. 33 secs., which was very fast running.

At the Civil Service championships, Jack Brown won the 1 mile, beating Len Eyre, while Bob Taylor won the 880 yds. in 1 min. 56.9 secs. At the newly-opened Croydon Track was held an Inter-County match and we had four winners at this meeting, as follows : Bob Taylor (Middx.), 880 ; Jack Brown (Kent), 1 mile ; T.
Also in 1953 he won the Civil Service mile title in a photo finish with Len Eyre, the Northern Champion, after finishing second on no less than four previous occasions.

Despite competing out of season against the in season Australian and New Zealand performers the Home Countries did well with fines wins by John Parlett in the 880 yds, Len Eyre in the 3 miles, Dorothy Tyler in the high jump, Tim Anderson in the pole vault and Jack Holden in the marathon.

The Great British middle distance event was of course dominated by Roger Bannister with new British mile and 1500 metre Records but perhaps a little disappointing in the Olympic Games. He was ably backed up by Bill Nankeville, four times British Champion, Len Eyre, John Parlett and Doug.
